study type: Retrospective observational study (combining questionnaire survey and registry data analysis)
exposure: Duration of expectant management after PROM (within 24h, 24-48h, >48h)
Facility management protocols (mechanical cervical dilation, oxytocin use, antibiotic administration for GBS)
cohort: Women expecting vaginal birth after term premature rupture of membrane (PROM) without clinical chorioamnionitis, managed at facilities participating in the Japan Perinatal Registry Network in 2016.
finding: Expectant management for up to 48 hours after term PROM did not increase the risk of postpartum fever or negatively affect neonatal outcomes compared to immediate labor induction.
mod_finding: The frequency of cesarean section did not differ among the three expectant management groups.
followup_time: N/A (outcomes measured at birth and short-term postpartum, but no specific duration mentioned)
